thread:
sachin: FYI seeing a weird skew in us-west-2 — GPUs at ~30% per-node but queue depth jumped to ~120 and short requests are sitting for >90s. feels like a scheduling front-lock.
maria: saw the same on perf-dash. lane=default FIFO is letting a few huge-context jobs hog the admission tokens. short jobs never get in.
devon: any logs? queue head info?
sachin: snippets from scheduler logs:
```
2026-03-17T08:12:03Z admission: grant request_id=abcd123 lane=default seq_len=75000 state=PENDING
2026-03-17T08:15:10Z admission: dequeue request_id=abcd123 node=gpu-12
2026-03-17T08:16:02Z admission: grant request_id=ef45 node=gpu-04 seq_len=256 state=ENQUEUED
```
maria: that seq_len=75000 is the killer. admission weight uses batch_size only, not seq_len. so one request is effectively front-of-line for minutes.
ana: (typo) i meant ana: quick mitigation idea: derive effective_weight = max(1, floor(seq_len / 1024)) so super long requests consume more tokens and won't block small ones.
leo: i can prototype a hotpatch that switches the admission token calc to include seq_len multiplier. small change in 35 lines. open to canary.
devon: another low-risk option: if a job waits >60s and there are smaller jobs in queue, temporarily bump small-job priority for X seconds (fairness ramp). cheaper than preemption.
sachin: preemption is riskier for long-running model state, prefer weight fix + short-job bump.
ops-bot: deploy initiated: scheduler-canary PR#3947 -> us-west-2 (rollout r-20260317-77). Monitoring subscribed: eng-infra, perf-dash. :rocket:
maria: canary metrics: within 70s queue depth 120 -> 22, p50 latency for short jobs down from 1.2s -> 0.25s, GPU distribution moved from 5 hot nodes to much more even spread.
sre-oncall: filing INC: INC-2026-03017. root cause: admission weight calc ignored seq_len leading to head-of-queue locking. mitigations: patch deployed to canary, follow-up tasks: unit tests, seq_len telemetry, graceful preempt plan. :white_check_mark:
sachin: created issue https://git.redwood/infra/issues/789 assigned to devon, leo. also adding postmortem notes. thanks everyone for the quick turn.
maria: :thumbsup: Lock closed in the hot path for now but let's get the tests + rollout vetted before full prod rollout.
